head: claude/mi102-manager-duties-queue-cadence
title: MI-102: canonize the manager's three base duties — two as checks, one refused
body:
## MI-102 — the manager's three base duties, canonized

Operator, 2026-09-03: *"that's one of the base functions of what a manager session is supposed to do. That needs to be canonized. It's not something you take upon yourself in the session."*

Two duties ship as checks. **The third is deliberately refused, with its reasoning** — the dispatch pre-authorized that: *"Refusing to mechanize it is a legitimate outcome; pretending to is not."*

---

## Duty 1 — the merge queue

⚠️ **`docs/claude/work/MERGE-QUEUE.json` DID NOT EXIST.** Not on main, not on any branch, not in any commit in history — I searched all three. It was cited to this session as *"the state of record … created today"* and used to settle a question. What existed was `docs/runbooks/merge-queue.md`, which is prose.

**The queue itself worked** — it unjammed the morning, and this is not a knock on it. It lived in one session's context, which is precisely the failure the ruling names. Created here, seeded with that day's actual queue.

**R8 enforces its one invariant: AT MOST ONE ENTRY `rebasing`.** Two sessions rebasing against the same moving `main` re-conflict each other by construction, and it is a state that looks fine to each session individually — which is why it needs a check rather than a convention. `blocked` additionally requires a named `blocked_on`, so *"not my turn"* and *"cannot go"* stay different facts.

**Measured harm before the queue existed:** 26 merges to main in a day, **19 (73%) touching a shared register**, two of them bare lease heartbeats — merges whose entire content is a timestamp. #10918 dirtied three times; ~16-minute CI runs voided before they finished.

---

## Duty 2 — the check-in cadence, as R7, graded on what HAPPENED

Per the dispatch: grade the observed gap between manager **actions**, never whether a cadence was *armed*.

**Population: 51 distinct heartbeat instants across every revision of `MANAGER-LEASE.json` → 48 consecutive SAME-HOLDER gaps** (a handover is not a lapse, and is excluded):

| min | p25 | **median** | p75 | p90 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 22 | **30** | 57 | 65 | 215 |

`>30min: 24/48 (50%)` · `>60min: 8/48 (17%)` · `>90min: 2/48 (4%)`

**30 is the median**, so a 30-minute rule fails half of everything this repo has ever done and gets deleted rather than fixed — the same reasoning R6 records, and why `heartbeat_target_minutes: 30` is a *target*, not this threshold. R7 uses the lease's own `ttl_minutes` (90), read from the file, with an anchor that does not come from the data at all: **takeover is time-based**, so a manager silent longer than one TTL has been quiet longer than the window another session may seize the lease in.

**Replayed on real history: fires on 3 of 59 gradeable commits (5%)** — gaps of 214, 131 and 100 minutes. Two of the three are same-holder *reclaims* after silence, which is the failure exactly.

### ⚠️ R7 would NOT have caught the failure that motivated it

This is written into the guard, not left to read as covered. The manager asked for R7 after its 11:04Z sweep silently never fired and #10923 sat green and mergeable from 11:01:05Z to 11:11Z with the **operator** noticing first. Measured that same day: **10 same-holder gaps, every one 15–35 minutes**, only 1 above 30. **The cadence that day was fine.** R7 grades whether the manager *checked in*, never whether it *acted on what was waiting*.

**Why the existing watcher missed it too** — measured by reading it: `pr_queue_latency.py` has `DEFAULT_THRESHOLD_HOURS = 6.0` and runs on cron `41 */6 * * *`. The event is below its threshold **and** below its sampling interval, each by a factor of 36. Worse, `grade_pr` computes quiescence as *hours since the last commit on the head branch* — so a just-green PR reads as **actively worked**, the opposite of "waiting on the manager". Filed as `BL-20260903-THE-PR-QUEUE-WATCHER-CANNOT-SEE-A-TEN-MINUTE-STALL`, including the harder half: the sweep was *armed* and silently didn't fire, so any fix whose liveness depends on a trigger firing inherits the same hole.

---

## Duty 3 — deliberately NOT mechanized

CI cannot read a conversation, so it cannot know feedback was given. Every design that survives that fact needs the graded party to first **write down** that it received something — and **omitting that write is free**. The check would grade exactly the subset where the manager already did the right thing, and be blind to the case that matters.

It is weaker than this repo's other partial checks: `session-registry-guard` at least joins **two independently-written records**; operator remarks have **no second record anywhere** — the decision round-trip covers operator *decisions*, not *remarks* — so there is nothing to join against and no denominator.

**It goes in the session-end `doc-freshness` discipline**, which already owns *"this session's material decisions actually landed in every durable surface they belong in"*.

⚠️ **And the one checkable sliver is already checked, which is why nothing new is added.** The last mile of duty 3 is *"a rule lands as canon WITH a mechanism"*, and a canon change naming a mechanism that does not exist is what `check_backlog_refs.py` catches for tracking ids. **That is not hypothetical — it is exactly what would have caught `MERGE-QUEUE.json`.** Grading the *name* against the filesystem needs no marker anybody could set.

---

## Proving the teeth

`--self-test` grows **13 → 19 cases**, every new rule with a plant **and** a control:

- **R7 plant** — 210 minutes since the previous heartbeat. The registry is kept *fresh* deliberately so R6 cannot fire and only R7 can; the test asserts `R6 not in fails`, because a plant that trips two rules proves neither.
- **R7 controls** — a 30-minute gap (the measured median) passes; a **handover** after a long silence passes, so an incoming manager is never failed for its predecessor's silence.
- **R8 plants** — two entries `rebasing`; `blocked` with an empty `blocked_on`.
- **R8 control** — one rebaser alongside `waiting`/`blocked`/`merged` passes.

## Verification

- `python3 scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main` → **PASS 64 · FAIL 0 · SKIP 21**, with **zero** guards not-selected.
- ⚠️ **The first run of that suite read `PASS 47 · FAIL 0` and was NOT a green result.** I had started it before committing, and the runner reported `17 NOT SELECTED because the work is UNCOMMITTED` *below* the summary — the 17 including `canonical-doc-coherence`, `ruff-lint`, `collapsed-state-guard`, `new-table-wiring-guard` and `writer-conformance-guard`, i.e. the guards most likely to have something to say about a `CLAUDE.md` edit and a new register file. I nearly reported it as green. Re-ran committed; that is where 64/0 comes from. Filed as `BL-20260903-RUN-GUARDS-PRINTS-FAIL-0-ON-A-RUN-IT-KNOWS-WAS-INCOMPLETE` — an incomplete run can only ever *under*-report failures, so it always looks like good news.

## Landing

`"landing": "hold"`. ⚠️ **The token is imperfect and disclosed**, as MI-95's was: `operator_asked_to_hold` names the *manager's* dispatch, not the operator's. Held because **this PR's own subject matter applies to it** — the queue says position 3, so it waits. R12's condition was checked and is **not** met.

## Two things for the manager

1. **The #10398 correction has no home.** You said it was written into `MERGE-QUEUE.json`; that file did not exist, and my seeded version records queue state only. If that note should survive, it needs somewhere to live.
2. **#10916 and #10920 are seeded with `branch: null, session_id: null`**, marked `UNRECORDED`. I don't know those values and won't invent them — but a queue entry nobody can resolve to a branch is half a record.
